summary: FTC treats unreasonable data security and misleading privacy claims as unfair or deceptive practices.
applies_to: For-profit repair/maintenance, personal care, laundry and similar businesses. Religious, grantmaking, civic and professional organizations organized as nonprofits are generally outside FTC jurisdiction (15 U.S.C. 44).

summary: Notify affected individuals (and often AGs) of breaches of personal information. Most state laws apply to nonprofits as well as businesses.
applies_to: Businesses and (in most states) nonprofits holding residents' PI.

citation: PCI Security Standards Council standard (contractual, not law)
summary: 12 requirement families for protecting cardholder data; enforced through card-brand and acquirer contracts.
applies_to: Any merchant or service provider that stores, processes or transmits payment card data.
size_thresholds: Validation level (SAQ vs. QSA ROC) depends on annual card-transaction volume under card-brand merchant-level programs. Those levels are set by the card brands and were not verified here.
status: v4.0.1 published June 11, 2024 (PCI SSC blog). Not a law. Check for any later revision.

summary: Any person that maintains or possesses consumer-report information for a business purpose must take reasonable measures when disposing of it.
applies_to: Employers, staffing firms and landlords that use background/consumer reports, plus their disposal vendors.

summary: Parental consent and written security program for personal information from children under 13.
applies_to: For-profit operators of child-directed online services (e.g., youth-activity apps).
size_thresholds: 'Operator' excludes nonprofits exempt from FTC Act Section 5 (16 CFR 312.2).

summary: Limits uses/disclosures of PHI, minimum necessary, individual rights, BAAs, and administrative safeguards (164.530(c)).
applies_to: Faith-based or civic organizations that operate clinics or health services and bill electronically in standard transactions; organizations sponsoring self-insured group health plans.
size_thresholds: Function-based (45 CFR 160.103); self-administered group health plans with fewer than 50 participants are excluded.
status: In force. The eCFR still shows the 2024 reproductive health care amendments (164.502(a)(5)(iii)); a federal court reportedly vacated them in June 2025. That status is not confirmed from a .gov source here.
